name: The Breakers

dates.note: Wikipedia: 'built between 1893 and 1895'; the survey: 'Date of erection: 189^ - July, 1895' (OCR; read as 1894); the node's exemplar says 1895. The survey also records the earlier house on the site, by Peabody and Stearns for Pierre Lorillard, altered for Vanderbilt in 1886 and 'destroyed by fire' on 25 November 1892.

quotes.text: 1. Over-all dimensions: About 250 feet by 150 feet; rectangular with kitchen ell at north corner; 3% stories.
quotes.page: HABS No. RI-339, Part II.B.1; no page marker legible in the span (the next legible is '(Page 5)')

quotes.text: 2. Foundations: The foundations are of cement made by Alsen's Port- land Cement Works, Hamburg, Germany. Approximately 10,000 barrels of concrete were used.
quotes.page: HABS No. RI-339, Part II.B.2; same span

quotes.text: 3. Wall construction. Buff Indiana limestone was employed for the walls. Brick and tile were used in some areas.
quotes.page: HABS No. RI-339, Part II.B.3; same span

quotes.text: k. Structural system: Steel beams form a lattice that carries the shallow brick and tile arches. The building is fireproof.
quotes.page: HABS No. RI-339, Part II.B.4; same span ('k.' is OCR for '4.')

quotes.text: 5. Chimneys: There are thirteen stone chimneys. The chimney caps are in form of Renaissance sarcophagi.
quotes.page: HABS No. RI-339, Part II.B.5; the marker '(Page 5)' follows

quotes.text: 6. Openings: a. The entrance doors are carved oak. Although very heavy, they are perfectly balanced on their hinges. The interior doors of the vestibule are topped by a semi-circular fan- light. Both the hand^wrought iron grille doors and fanlight are glazed. In order to facilitate cleaning, the door leaves open like pages in a book, giving clear access to the plate glass panel within. Entry onto the loggia fron the house is through French windows in the oortile, or great hall, billiard room, and morning room. There are French windows that open to the southwest terrace from the music room. The French windows have semi-circular top lights
quotes.page: HABS No. RI-339 (Page 5), Part II.B.6; the chunk ends mid-sentence

quotes.text: 2. Stairways: Five marble steps in the entrance hall ascend to the main floor level. The marble grand staircase rises from the great ■ hall floor to a landing and thence in opposite directions to second- ary landings and thence in twin flights to the westerly second-floor gallery of the great hall. The flights sweep upward in graceful curves on open arches. The closed marble stringers are carved in a Vitruvian wave motif and are surmounted by elaborate wrought iron and bronze railings. There is a fountain within the arch below the first flight.
rooms of "The Breakers" enclose a two story cortile and loggia that face southeast to the sea. 2. Condition of fabric: The building and its furnishings-: are in excellent condition.
